neighbours.label: the pieces of Perseid(s) and Persephone ('Per|se|ids', 'Per|se|phone')
fire: Stargazers love the Perseids because they are so bright.
In the myth, Demeter mourned for Persephone all winter.
A camera caught a Perseid fireball over the desert.
Orpheus begged Persephone to release his wife.
Each August the Perseids light up the night sky.
Her poem compares spring to the return of Persephone.
We drove out of town to watch the Perseid shower.
The vase shows Persephone seated beside Hades.
quiet: Stargazers love the Leonids because they are so bright.

A camera caught a large fireball over the desert.
Orpheus begged Hades to release his wife.
Each December the Geminids light up the night sky.
